VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The proof handles degenerate intervals explicitly (step 1.1). Subdividing a finite interval cover shows that max ℓ_r can be made arbitrarily small without increasing total length, so the required “sufficiently small” condition is always attainable. The stacked squares form a finite axis‑parallel rectangle cover of C×[0,1] with total area ≤ ∑ℓ_r + 2(max ℓ_r)∑ℓ_r; choosing the cover so that this sum is < ε is possible for every ε > 0. Hence the slab has Jordan outer content 0 and is Jordan measurable with content 0.
